title: fix: raise mysqldump max-allowed-packet to avoid TLS eof on wide rows
body:
## Summary

A MySQL dump failed mid-table with:

```
mysqldump failed: exit status 3: mysqldump: Error 2026: TLS/SSL error:
unexpected eof while reading when dumping table `data` at row: 124150
```

This is the classic signature of a **single wide row exceeding `max_allowed_packet`**: when mysqldump asks for a row larger than its packet buffer, the server tears down the TCP connection without a TLS `close_notify`, which OpenSSL reports as `Error 2026 ... unexpected eof`. The dump aborts at the exact row that's too big (here row 124150 of a table literally named `data` — almost certainly a large BLOB/JSON/TEXT column). It is **not** an FTPS/network issue: the dump is written to a local temp file first (`pipeline_dump.go`), so the upload backpressure path isn't involved.

mysqldump's built-in default `--max-allowed-packet` is only ~24 MiB. We never overrode it, so any row above that killed the dump.

Fix: pass `--max-allowed-packet=1G` (MySQL's own maximum) by default, overridable per source:

```
backup.mogenius.io/extra-max-allowed-packet: "512M"
```

Arg building is extracted into `buildDumpArgs()` so the flag set is unit-testable without exec'ing the binary.

```go
maxPacket := d.cfg.Extra["max-allowed-packet"]
if maxPacket == "" { maxPacket = "1G" }
args = append(args, "--max-allowed-packet="+maxPacket)
```

Caveat documented in code + README: the **server's** `max_allowed_packet` must also be large enough to emit such a row; if rows are genuinely huge, it must be raised server-side too. Raising the client ceiling fixes the common case where the client buffer is the limiter.

## Changes
- `src/dumper/mysql/mysql.go` — add `--max-allowed-packet` (default `1G`, override via `extra-max-allowed-packet`); extract `buildDumpArgs()`.
- `src/dumper/mysql/mysql_test.go` — cover the default flag set and the override.
- `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — document the new `extra-max-allowed-packet` tunable and the Error 2026 remedy.

## Testing
- `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, `go vet ./...` — all green
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
